subject.title: sec (5/9): reject unsafe targets on the Windows host shell

question: Should ClawScan intentionally reject all Windows host-shell targets containing `%`, `!`, or double quotes, even when those characters occur in an otherwise legitimate existing target path?
rationale: The proposed behavior is a conservative command-injection defense, but it changes a supported `--sandbox off` workflow for existing Windows users and cannot be accepted solely as a mechanical test decision.

options.title: Accept the fail-closed guard
options.body: Merge the narrow rejection behavior and document the Docker sandbox or a compatible target path as the supported recovery path.

options.title: Require a different Windows execution design
options.body: Pause this change until the scanner command can receive targets without `cmd.exe` interpolation or a compatible argument-passing mechanism is available.

recommendation.title: Accept the fail-closed guard
recommendation.body: Merge the narrow rejection behavior and document the Docker sandbox or a compatible target path as the supported recovery path.

likelyOwner.reason: They introduced the merged user-defined scanner execution surface and authored the focused hardening series.
